# llms.txt — Project Design | Love-Driven Dev — pjdhiro

> This file helps AI assistants and language models understand the structure and content of this site.

## Site Overview

This is the hub site of pjdhiro presenting **Project Design Theory (プロジェクトデザイン論)** — the practice of designing not only projects but the very methods by which projects are run and managed (プロジェクトの実行・管理の方法そのものを対象化し、構想・設計する営み). It encompasses both Doing (actions) and Being (phenomena).

- **Primary Language**: Japanese (日本語), with English summaries
- **Site URL**: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/
- **Topics**: Designing project-management methods, Project Design Theory, Love-Driven Development, 事業構想 (Business Planning), PMBOK Extension, Emotional Processing, Creativity Structure, Intersubjectivity, Negative Capability

## Who This Is For

People who want to **design how a project is run and managed**, not just pick an existing method and apply it:
project managers, business owners, team leads, and researchers of project-management methodology
(プロジェクト管理手法・進め方そのものをどう設計するかに関心がある人).

## Questions This Site Answers

- **What does it mean to design a project-management method itself?** — Instead of only selecting and applying an existing method such as PMBOK, the way a given project is run and managed becomes a design object. Project Design defines two objects: (1) envisioning, designing, and executing a project; (2) envisioning and designing the method of executing and managing it.
- **How does it relate to PMBOK?** — It extends rather than replaces it. Environmental adaptation (material conditions), covered in detail by PMBOK 7th edition, is taken as a premise. On top of that, Being (what is happening) is added to Doing (what we do); emotions become a design concern rather than one element of stakeholder management; communication is designed as intersubjective experience, not only information transfer; creativity is structured with the Five-Stage Model.
- **What gets added to the design scope?** — Project work is split into environmental adaptation (material) and communication (non-material); communication is split into information processing and emotional processing. Emotional processing — emotional contagion, emotional metacognition, personal boundaries, acceptance, value — is the main focus. Kesson-Driven Thinking (starting from noticing what is missing) is used as a thinking method.
- **Where does it apply?** — Mainly for-profit and non-profit business, but the framework applies to any purposeful activity that repeats envisioning, decision-making, execution, and adjustment (research, life, etc.).
- **Where to start?** — Concrete explorations: team size (3 and 7) and emotions and relationships as flows (readers below).
- **Status** — Exploratory and unfinished; the inquiry is published in progress, including retracted readings.

## Core Concepts

### Project Design (プロジェクトデザイン)

A framework for designing not just projects but the methods of project execution themselves. Applicable to business planning (事業構想) across profit and non-profit enterprises. It extends traditional project management (PMBOK) by incorporating emotional processing, communication, and creative emergence as first-class design concerns.

### Love-Driven Development (Love駆動開発)

A phenomenon where relationships, emotions, and intent become the driving forces of a project — beyond rational planning and resource allocation.

## How It Differs from PMBOK

| Aspect | Traditional PM (PMBOK) | Project Design |
|--------|----------------------|----------------|
| Scope | Doing (deliverables, tasks) | Doing + Being (phenomena, emergence) |
| Emotions | Side effect to manage | First-class design concern |
| Creativity | Outside scope | Structured via Five-Stage Model |
| Communication | Information transfer | Intersubjective encounter |
| Human-AI | Tool usage | Co-design partnership |

Public explainer pages, written to be uniquely readable by LLMs without external context. Each states its verification status honestly, including retracted readings.

### なぜ 3 と 7 だけが特別なのか — 可除代数‑意識/組織仮説
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/three-and-seven.html
- One-line: From the felt experience "teams work best at 3, cap at 7" and a two-axis view of consciousness, the page asks whether "multiplicative management" could literally be rotation multiplication — and walks the ladder of division algebras (ℝ→ℂ→ℍ→𝕆, Hurwitz's theorem) against team-size research, keeping theorem / strong reading / weak reading strictly separated.
- Status: exploratory hypothesis with explicit falsification conditions; failed strong readings are published, not hidden.
- Paper (Markdown source, ja, non-peer-reviewed, CC BY 4.0): https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/blob/main/pd/knowledge/research/two-axis-closure/PAPER-division-algebra-ja.md — academic-format version of the same findings, with references (reading-depth annotated) and 20 re-runnable verification scripts.
- Paper (Markdown source, en translation): https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/blob/main/pd/knowledge/research/two-axis-closure/PAPER-division-algebra-en.md

### Love駆動開発と呼びたいもの β
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/love-driven-dev.html
- One-line: Love-Driven Development is what pjdhiro wants to call, as a whole, the driving sources, structures and processes overlooked behind the phenomenon called a project. It is at work before a vision is put into words. Management studies have written about the acts of development (envisioning, planning, moving — Doing). The page writes about the unseen part before them, the way gravity has been described by how things move around it: through gravity, vortices, survival and trust signals, kesson (felt lack) and value creation, calling on four related inquiries.
- Status: under construction (seventh draft). Written by Claude; pjdhiro set the questions and judges whether it fits.
- Grounds: Love-Driven Development is pjdhiro's theory from naive personal experience. The grounds behind its claims are one person's first-person experience, not statistics drawn from many people. Cited research is material for conveying that experience, not proof of it; where experience and research disagree, neither is bent to fit the other and the gap is kept as an open question.
- English version: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/love-driven-dev-en.html — "What I Want to Call Love-Driven Development β", translated by Claude from the Japanese version 1.234 (2026-11-18). It asks two questions, "What drives us to do projects? What drives us to live?" and "Why do we try to become something different from what we were?", in seven parts: the views so far; similar shapes (the five stages of creation, gravity, physics); how people interpret the world; how the mind feels trust and reassurance; what Love is; what happens inside development; and what I want to call Love-Driven Development (the definition, education, philosophy and Zen, where the view is useful, training and practice). The Japanese page may be newer; the English page is updated from time to time.

### 心理的安全性とは
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/psychological-safety.html
- One-line: What does the term psychological safety point to? The page sets pjdhiro's view — a state without psychological safety is defense against anxiety (psychological defense mechanisms), and what we call high psychological safety is a state of mature defense — against the maturity levels of defense (Vaillant, Perry) and the defenses of each stage of ego development (Cook-Greuter). It opens with a table of how "Let's raise psychological safety" tends to sound at each stage, traces the term from Lewin (1947) to Edmondson (1999), places shame anxiety within that literature, sets out absence of threat and cues of safety and the difference from trust, and looks at why workplace measures miss the mark, one common misunderstanding at a time.
- Status: under construction. Written by Claude; pjdhiro's views are quoted and marked.
- English version: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/psychological-safety-en.html — "What Is Psychological Safety", translated by Claude from the Japanese version 1.000 (2026-11-14). The Japanese page may be newer.

### 愛は、重力に似ていないか — 動かず、何もなく、自分からは見えないのに、すべてを回す中心
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/gravity-love.html
- One-line: Is love like gravity? The interest is the driving force that moves things around: we usually think what moves is what drives, but perhaps it is the unmoving center. A management / project-design reader; in the second half it gives a hypothetical answer to "what is a leader's role?". pjdhiro's reading: a leader's role is decision-making, yet the role of their being is unexplored. It looks for that by (1) splitting "decision-making" the way metacognition splits the self — pjdhiro likens this to probing an electron ever more finely until the classical picture gives way to the quantum one — so that a Being layer (an unmoving center) appears beneath the movement of deciding; (2) using the center of a gravity well (does not move, holds nothing, cannot see itself) and (3) love as auxiliary lines; (4) asking whether love and the leader are alike; (5) leaving a root question open: humans exist between persons, and the self exists where one divides oneself.
- Status: first edition (2026-11-01). Physics, logic of viewpoint, metaphor and speculation are separated. Precedents: Aristotle (Metaphysics Λ7), Dante (Paradiso 33.145), Wittgenstein (Tractatus 5.633), Laozi ch.11/17, Watsuji Tetsurō (ningen as "between persons"), the Yogācāra four-part theory of cognition (Hossō school), Nishida Kitarō (to know is to mirror the self within the self).

### パース「進化的な愛」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-evolutionary-love-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "Evolutionary Love" (The Monist 3(2), January 1893, pp.176–200), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce distinguishes three modes of evolution — by fortuitous variation (tychasm), by mechanical necessity (anancasm) and by creative love (agapasm) — and holds that the first two are degenerate forms of the third, setting the "Gospel of Christ" against the "Gospel of Greed".
- Status: the original text was checked character by character against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content); the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original. A final chapter, apart from the translation and under construction, collects pjdhiro's interpretations of and reactions to the paper.

### パース「心の法則」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-law-of-mind-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "The Law of Mind" (The Monist 2(4), July 1892, pp.533–559), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce states that there is but one law of mind: ideas tend to spread continuously and to affect certain others; in spreading they lose intensity but gain generality. He names the doctrine of continuity synechism, defines continuity against Kant and Cantor, and treats time, feeling, habit, the forms of inference, personality and communication.
- Status: the original text was checked character by character against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content); the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original.

### パース「人間のガラスのような本質」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-glassy-essence-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "Man's Glassy Essence" (The Monist 3(1), October 1892, pp.1–22), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce frames a molecular theory of matter and of protoplasm (the virial, Van der Waals, Amagat, dissociation), explains liquefaction, growth, habit-taking and feeling from it, holds that chance is the outward aspect of what within itself is feeling, and ends with personality as a coördination of feelings and the possibility of corporate personality.
- Status: the original text was checked against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content), restoring the formulas; the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original.

### ケーラス「パース氏の必然論への猛攻」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/carus-onslaught-on-necessity-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Paul Carus's "Mr. Charles S. Peirce's Onslaught on the Doctrine of Necessity" (The Monist 2(4), July 1892, pp.560–582), the editor's reply to Peirce's "The Doctrine of Necessity Examined", with the original under each paragraph. Carus likens Peirce to Hume, argues that causation is not mere sequence, that necessity in thought presupposes necessity in facts and that laws are not inexplicable, and calls Peirce's view that absolute chance begets order "the weakest point of Mr. Peirce's system" (p.576), a phrase Peirce quotes in "Evolutionary Love" (1893).
- Status: there is no Wikisource transcription; the original was built from the OCR and checked against all 23 pages of the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content). The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

Only this excerpt of the book is translated.

Only this excerpt of the book is translated.

### マンデヴィル『蜂の寓話』（1714）の詩「ぶつぶつ言う蜂の巣」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/mandeville-grumbling-hive-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, stanza by stanza, of Bernard Mandeville's poem "The Grumbling Hive: or, Knaves turn'd Honest" as printed at the head of The Fable of the Bees: or, Private Vices, Publick Benefits (London, 1714), pp.1–20, the book Peirce cites in "Evolutionary Love" (1893) ¶14 for the claim that private vices are public benefits, with the original under each stanza. Only the poem is translated, not the Remarks or essays.
- Status: the original follows the 1714 edition, checked line by line against the page images of the Internet Archive scan, using the Wikisource transcription of the 1705 pamphlet as a base; differences from 1705 and the book's errata are noted. The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

### ヘルムホルツ『力の保存について』（1847）を、日本語で読む

Reimer, 1847; 72 pages, with the erratum), which Peirce calls "the sublime discovery of the conservation of energy by Helmholtz in 1847" in "Evolutionary Love" (1893) ¶20, with the German original under each paragraph.

### クラウジウス「熱の動力について」（1850）を、日本語で読む

### マンセル『宗教的思考の限界』（1858）の序文を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/mansel-limits-of-religious-thought-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of the first Preface (pp.v–x) of Henry Longueville Mansel's The Limits of Religious Thought Examined in Eight Lectures (the Bampton Lectures of 1858; Oxford: J. Wright for John Murray, 1858), in which Mansel says that Sir William Hamilton's principle that "the Unconditioned is incognisable and inconceivable" suggested the principal part of his inquiries, with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce mentions "Dean Mansell's injudicious advocacy" of Hamilton in "Evolutionary Love" (1893) ¶20.
- Status: only the Preface is translated, not the eight lectures or the notes; Peirce names neither the book nor a page, and Claude chose the Preface. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan. The two Hamilton quotations were checked against Hamilton's Discussions (1852), pp.12 and 15. The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

### ミル『ハミルトン哲学の検討』（1865）の第 VII 章を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/mill-examination-of-hamilton-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Chapter VII (pp.88–105) of John Stuart Mill's An Examination of Sir William Hamilton's Philosophy (London: Longman, Green, Longman, Roberts & Green, 1865; public domain; English), "The Philosophy of the Conditioned, as applied by Mr. Mansel to the Limits of Religious Thought", in which Mill examines Mansel's argument that God's attributes cannot be known in the sense of human goodness and justice, and answers that he will call no being good who is not good in the sense he applies to his fellow-creatures.
- Status: only Chapter VII is translated; Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) names neither the book nor a page, and Claude chose this chapter as Mill's direct answer to Mansel. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan of the first edition. The passages of Mansel and Hamilton that Mill quotes were not checked against their books. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### ハミルトン「無条件者の哲学について」（1829）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/hamilton-philosophy-of-the-unconditioned-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Sir William Hamilton's article "Philosophy of the Unconditioned; in reference to Cousin's Doctrine of the Infinito-Absolute" (Edinburgh Review 50, October 1829; public domain; English), taken from the revised reprint in Hamilton's Discussions on Philosophy and Literature, Education and University Reform (London, 1852), pp.1–37, in which Hamilton examines Victor Cousin's claim that the Unconditioned is known immediately by reason, and answers that the Unconditioned is incognisable and inconceivable, that to think is to condition, and that a "learned ignorance" is perhaps the consummation of knowledge.
- Status: the whole article and its footnotes are translated; Hamilton's 1852 additions are kept in square brackets. Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) names neither the article nor a page; Claude chose it as the work that Mansel names in his Preface and that Mill attacks. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan of the 1852 volume. The Latin, Greek, French and German quotations and the references in the footnotes were not checked against their sources. The 1829 magazine text was not compared sentence by sentence. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

## Using This Repository for a Love-Driven Development Review

To review a paper or text using the view of "Love駆動開発と呼びたいもの β" as the yardstick, use an LLM that can fetch the repository (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) and follow the README section 「Love駆動開発の視点でレビューに使うとき」: https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory#love駆動開発の視点でレビューに使うとき
- Fetch: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory`
- Read in order: the reader's Markdown source `pd/knowledge/research/love-driven-dev/READER-love-driven-dev.md` (to the end), then `docs/rules/stance.md` (pjdhiro's view and way of judging), then `docs/rules/corrections.md` (misreadings LLMs tend to repeat).
- The conditions and nuances of the view (what each statement answered, which readings were rejected) are in those rule files, not in the public pages. This file and the public pages alone are not enough for such a review.
- Love-Driven Development is pjdhiro's theory from naive personal experience, offered as a hypothesis. A review written this way is the LLM's reading, not pjdhiro's judgment.
